name: Interpretation of Tongues
essenceStatement: The Spirit-given ability to make a tongue intelligible to the gathered body for its edification.
workingDefinition: The Spirit-given ability to render a spoken tongue into the language of the gathered church so that what was said becomes intelligible and edifying for the body. Interpretation is not literal translation; Paul's word implies the conveyance of the meaning, sense, and direction of the tongue rather than a word-for-word rendering. The gift exists specifically to make the corporate exercise of tongues fruitful for the church -- without interpretation, Paul explicitly forbids public tongues (1 Corinthians 14:28). The gift is the necessary complement to tongues in the gathered setting.
diagnosticChallenge: This gift is even less commonly addressed than tongues in contemporary church culture. It is easily confused with general spiritual sensitivity, the impression that one knows what a public tongue meant, or the prepared interpretation offered without genuine Spirit-given empowerment. The signature of the gift is the consistent ability, when a public tongue is spoken, to render its meaning in the language of the body in ways that produce edification, encouragement, or instruction -- and that subsequent testing of the interpretation confirms it as from the Spirit.

manifestationWitnesses.text: If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three, and each in turn, and let someone interpret.
manifestationWitnesses.note: Paul's regulation for corporate tongues necessarily implies the gift of interpretation. The instruction 'let someone interpret' assumes that the Spirit has gifted at least one believer in the gathering with the corresponding ability. Without this gift in operation, the gift of tongues cannot be exercised publicly according to scripture.

manifestationWitnesses.text: Therefore, one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
manifestationWitnesses.note: Paul's instruction that the tongues-speaker should also pray to interpret. The two gifts may operate in the same believer, and Paul's framing suggests that the integrated exercise is the most edifying form. The gift of interpretation is sometimes given to the same believer who speaks in tongues, and sometimes to a different believer in the gathered body.

stewardshipCharge.text: Let all things be done for building up.
stewardshipCharge.note: Paul's controlling principle for the use of all charismatic gifts in the gathered church. Interpretation, in particular, exists to make tongues edifying. The gift's purpose is the body's building up. Interpretation that does not produce edification has either misread the tongue or has drifted from the gift's scriptural function.

directExperienceQuestion: When a public tongue has been spoken in a gathered context, have you received and offered an interpretation -- a Spirit-given understanding of the tongue's meaning, rendered in the language of the body -- that the gathered church received as edifying and that has been confirmed by other gifted believers as consistent with the Spirit's work?
fruitfulnessQuestion: When you have offered an interpretation, how often has the gathered body been visibly edified, encouraged, or instructed by what you shared -- and how often has subsequent testing by mature believers confirmed that the interpretation was from the Spirit rather than from your own thinking?

bodyApplication.where: The gift of interpretation functions almost exclusively in corporate worship contexts where the gift of tongues is also being exercised publicly -- typically in churches and gatherings that honor Paul's regulations and practice the charismatic gifts in order. In churches that do not practice the corporate exercise of tongues, this gift has fewer occasions to manifest, though some believers who carry it report receiving impressions of meaning when they hear tongues spoken in personal prayer contexts or recorded ministries. The gift is uncommon, even more so than tongues itself, and its operation requires the corresponding presence of public tongues to be exercised meaningfully.
bodyApplication.whatItLooksLike: The believer who consistently receives and offers interpretations that the gathered body receives as edifying. The interpreter whose work over time has been confirmed by mature, accountable leadership in their church as Spirit-given rather than constructed. An interpretation-gifted believer functioning well operates under the same regulations Paul gives for prophecy -- the interpretation is submitted, tested, and weighed by the elders or pastoral leadership of the church (1 Corinthians 14:29). They are quick to say 'I think the Spirit gave me this' rather than 'thus saith the Lord,' and they welcome correction.
bodyApplication.distortions: This gift, when distorted, can produce some of the most damaging dynamics in charismatic worship. It can become prepared performance: the interpreter who offers the same generic 'interpretation' regardless of what was actually spoken in tongues. It can become competitive: multiple believers offering competing interpretations without submission to testing. It can become a tool of control: the leader who interprets others' tongues in ways that direct the congregation, exact compliance, or assert authority. The corrective is Paul's framework throughout 1 Corinthians 14: order, accountability, testing, and the orienting purpose of the body's edification.
bodyApplication.pairings: Interpretation pairs primarily with Tongues -- the gift it complements and makes corporately useful. It also pairs with Prophecy (the gift it most closely resembles in function, since the rendered interpretation often takes the form of a word for the body) and with Discernment of Spirits (which protects the interpreter from offering interpretations that are not from God).

formationOutput.active:
The Spirit's work in you through the gift of interpretation is to make the gift of tongues edifying for the gathered body. This is what Paul describes in 1 Corinthians 14:13, 26-28: the interpreter renders the meaning of the tongue so that the church may be built up. The gift is uncommon and is exercised under regulation. It is also vital -- without it in operation, the gift of tongues cannot be exercised publicly according to scripture.

The stewardship of this gift requires the same accountability framework that governs prophecy. Submit your interpretations to the testing of mature leadership in your church. Refuse the temptation to offer prepared or generic interpretations. Welcome correction. Resist any context that pressures you to interpret without genuine Spirit-given impression, or that uses interpretation as a tool of control. The gift's purpose is the body's edification, and its faithful exercise requires the humility to be wrong, to be tested, and to be silent when the Spirit has not given you a word.
formationOutput.anchorScriptureText: Let all things be done for building up.
formationOutput.weeklyPractice: If your church practices the corporate exercise of tongues and you have been called to interpret, continue in faithful submission to your pastor and elders. When an interpretation comes to you, write it down before sharing it where possible. Submit it for testing. Welcome correction. If your church does not practice corporate tongues, exercise the gift in the contexts where it has been confirmed and remain attentive to the Spirit's leading without seeking opportunities the Spirit has not opened.

edgeCases.emerging: Your responses suggest you may have received impressions of meaning when tongues have been spoken, but the gift has not yet been confirmed through consistent, edifying exercise under accountable leadership. Submit any impressions to your pastor or to mature, accountable believers before sharing them publicly. Practice the discipline of writing down what you sense, testing it carefully, and only offering it when it holds up under scrutiny. The gift, if it is real, will be confirmed over time through the body's edification.
edgeCases.notPresent: This gift is not where the Spirit has chosen to work in your life. The gift of interpretation is uncommon, and its absence in a believer's life is no commentary on their faithfulness or maturity. Honor the interpretation-gifted believers in your community when they emerge, and look to the gifts where the Spirit is more clearly at work in you. The Spirit's gifts are distributed as he wills, and that distribution can shift -- the picture is of this season, not a permanent verdict.
